text:
Situation: Midazolam hydrochloride has been on FDA's drug shortage list since 2020-04-02 and remains current as of 2026-10-21. Corvale General holds a 1 mg/mL, 5 mL vial line with only 9.9 days on hand (72 vials). Corvale East holds the same strength and size with 15.1 days on hand (84 vials). Other sites have adequate stock across multiple presentations.

Why (FDA record): FDA first posted the shortage on 2020-04-02. The label for NDC 00409230505 lists Hospira, Inc. (FEI 1925262) and Pfizer Healthcare India Private Limited (FEI 3008316085) as registered plants. FDA inspection 1064827 at the Hospira plant ended 2018-08-15, was classified OAI, and the classification letter is dated 2020-04-22. A Warning Letter was issued to that plant on 2020-03-25. FDA inspection 1106244 at the Pfizer India plant ended 2019-09-06, was classified OAI, and the classification letter is dated 2020-05-25.

Our position: The shortage is longstanding and multi-facility. Internal redistribution can close the gap at Corvale General without new purchasing risk. Three alternative manufacturers (B. Braun, Belcher, Civica) are not on FDA's shortage list today, but their labels name no plants we can verify.

Recommended actions:
1. Transfer 6 vials of midazolam hydrochloride 1 mg/mL, 5 mL from Corvale East to Corvale General — raises Corvale General to 11 days on hand; Corvale East retains two weeks. Approval: Pharmacy Director; controlled-substance transfer record (Schedule III-V) required.
2. Monitor days-on-hand at all sites weekly and report to P&T at next meeting. Approval: Pharmacy Director.
3. If redistribution cannot sustain supply, evaluate qualified alternative suppliers with verifiable plant registrations. Approval: P&T Committee and Pharmacy Director.

Not recommended: Purchasing from B. Braun Medical Inc., Belcher Pharmaceuticals, LLC, or Civica, Inc. at this time due to inability to verify manufacturing sites.
